blocks.text: As container counts grew, the problem shifted from running one container to running many across hosts: Compose handles multi-container apps on one host, Swarm added simple clustering, and Kubernetes became the standard orchestrator.

rows: Simple YAML, great for dev and small prod
No multi-node HA, no rolling updates
Kubernetes (announced 2014, 1.0 in 2015; from Google's Borg experience)
Reconciliation, rolling updates, autoscaling, huge ecosystem

items: Scheduling containers onto nodes by resources.
Local dev and single-VM services: Compose.
Multi-node, HA, autoscaling: Kubernetes or a managed container platform (ECS, Cloud Run, Container Apps).

blocks.text: Q: "Compose vs Kubernetes?" A: "Compose defines and runs a multi-container app on one host, ideal for dev and simple deployments. Kubernetes schedules and continuously reconciles workloads across many nodes, with rolling updates, autoscaling and self-healing, at much higher operational cost."

items: Kubernetes = cluster reconciliation; it won the orchestrator race.
